h1:
Trang Roast Pork (Moo Yang)
10 Crispy-Skin Morning Shops Locals Eat
intro: Trang is the one place in Thailand where roast pork is a breakfast, not an evening drinking snack. Locals get up, sit down at a dim sum shop, order a plate of crispy-skin moo yang, dip it in a sweet-savory sauce, and wash it down with hot coffee. These are the shops people here actually go to, with the area, opening hours and the prices you'll find right now.

blocks.html: Trang roast pork isn't like roast pork anywhere else. They roast the whole pig in a charcoal oven, marinate it with Chinese spices until the meat turns sweet first and savory after, and get a skin that crisps up into sheets — tap it and you hear it snap. To eat it, they chop it into small pieces and dip it in a sauce each shop keeps to its own recipe. Trang moo yang even holds a GI registration (geographical indication), because the flavor and the way it's made are genuinely tied to this town.

What a lot of people don't realize is that the real roast pork shops in Trang open early and sell out fast. The famous market vendors start roasting in the dead of night, set up around 5am, and by mid-morning they're done. If you're set on the best ones, you'll have to drag yourself out of bed a little early.

blocks.text: The Trang Roast Pork Shops Locals Actually Eat At

blocks.html: We've ranked them by where local word-of-mouth and the actual reviews line up — a mix of market vendors you'll queue for, long-running shops in town, and places that stay open later in case you can't make it out early. Prices are rough figures we found and may shift with the season.

items.name: Ko Phao Roast Pork (Trang Municipal Fresh Market)
items.blurb: The one Trang locals call the most famous of all, tucked inside the municipal fresh market in the middle of town. Crisp on the outside, sweet and juicy inside. People line up before the stall is even set out — they start roasting from 1am and it sells out very quickly, so even running a little late means missing out. You can call ahead to reserve.
items.meta: Municipal fresh market (in town) · Open ~6:00am–10:00am (sells out fast)

items.name: Trang Moo Yang
items.blurb: A long-running roast pork and dim sum shop on Huai Yot Road, open most of the day, good for anyone who'd rather sit down and eat in peace without fighting for a spot in line. The small plates are fairly priced, the flavor is sweet-leading and well-rounded with their own dipping sauce, and there are rib noodles, spring rolls and dim sum to order alongside.
items.meta: Huai Yot Rd, Thap Thiang · Open morning to late

items.name: Ko Jiu Roast Pork
items.blurb: Another vendor in the municipal market that people scramble to buy from. Opens very early, crisp skin and tender meat, and locals buy it by the kilo to take home. Come before 9am if you don't want to be disappointed.

items.name: Ban Bua Bok Roast Pork
items.blurb: On Phetkasem Road in the Na Ta Luang area, open from 5:30am. This one leans toward thin, crisp skin with sweet, fragrant meat. It's been going for over ten years and ships nationwide too, so it's a good one to pick up as a gift to take back.
items.meta: Phetkasem Rd, Na Ta Luang · Open ~5:30am–12:00pm

items.name: Ko Sui Roast Pork
items.blurb: An old shop going on 40 years on Phetkasem Road, working from a marinade recipe passed down the family. Crisp skin, firm meat, with dim sum and sausage sold alongside. Closed Tuesdays.
items.meta: Phetkasem Rd, Na Ta Luang · Open ~6:00am–1:00pm (closed Tue)

items.name: Ko Kae Roast Pork
items.blurb: Out in Huai Yot district, a bit outside the city, but people are willing to drive there for a secret recipe handed down for nearly a hundred years. Sweet, well-rounded meat and crisp skin. Closed Sundays, and it sells out quickly in the afternoon.
items.meta: Phetkasem Rd, Huai Yot district · Open ~7:00am–2:00pm (closed Sun)

items.name: Tha Do Roast Pork
items.blurb: The most wallet-friendly on the list, over in the Na Wong area of Huai Yot. Golden skin, soft and fragrant meat, and the people around there eat it regularly. Opens very early, from 5:30am.
items.meta: Na Wong, Huai Yot district · Open ~5:30am–12:30pm

items.name: Ko Kuang Roast Pork
items.blurb: Over in Wang Khiri, Huai Yot, this one opens later and runs into the evening — handy if you can't make it out in time for the in-town vendors. Its own marinade recipe; worth reserving ahead if you want a lot. Closed Wednesdays.
items.meta: Wang Khiri, Huai Yot district · Open ~6:00am–5:00pm (closed Wed)

items.name: Pong O-Cha
items.blurb: A dim sum and roast pork shop Trang locals know well, with branches that open long and close later than the others. Good if you want roast pork with dim sum mid-morning or for an evening meal. Order the roast pork by the plate with tea or coffee.
items.meta: In Trang town · Open long, into the evening (varies by branch)

items.name: Sin Jiu (in front of Chaloem Trang Cinema)
items.blurb: A decades-old coffee and dim sum shop with an old-school feel. The roast pork is sold alongside tea, coffee, dim sum and noodles. A nice spot to sit and soak in a real Trang-style breakfast.
items.meta: By Chaloem cinema, in town · Opens early
items.price: Dim sum ~20–30/basket · roast pork plate from ~80

blocks.title: Want the best ones? Get up early
blocks.html: Market vendors like Ko Phao and Ko Jiu selling out before 10am is completely normal. If you're serious about eating there, go before 8am to be safe. Can't face the early start? Aim for the later-closing shops like Ko Kuang or Pong O-Cha instead.

blocks.text: How to Eat Trang Roast Pork Like a Local

blocks.html: Trang locals don't eat roast pork on its own — they eat it as a full breakfast set. Here's how to order so it feels like you're sitting down with a friend from Trang.

items: Roast pork with the dipping sauce — the heart of it is each shop's own sauce, sweet and savory and balanced. Chop the pork into small pieces and dip one bite at a time.
A few small baskets of dim sum — order har gow, pork siu mai and bao to share; they're the inseparable partner to the roast pork.
Old-style coffee or hot tea — Trang dim sum shops brew strong coffee that cuts the richness of the roast pork nicely.
Dim sum with a cracked egg / shrimp siu mai — if you find a shop making it fresh, ordering more won't let you down.

blocks.text: Which Areas Have the Roast Pork Shops

items.name: Trang Municipal Fresh Market (in town)
items.blurb: Right in the center of Thap Thiang, home to the famous market vendors like Ko Phao and Ko Jiu. Buy it fresh and carry it out. Come as early as you can.

items.name: Phetkasem Road / Na Ta Luang
items.blurb: A run of dine-in roast pork shops like Ban Bua Bok and Ko Sui. They open early, and parking is easier than in the market.

items.name: Huai Yot District
items.blurb: Outside town toward Huai Yot you'll find old-recipe vendors like Ko Kae, Tha Do and Ko Kuang. People are happy to drive out for the traditional recipes.

blocks.text: Taking It Home as a Gift

blocks.html: Trang roast pork travels well — many shops vacuum-pack it and ship nationwide. If you're taking it a long way, tell the shop you want the ship-ready pack and they'll sort it for you. The classic local pairing to bring back is Chinese pastry (the Soi 9 maker is well known), to eat with tea or coffee at home.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Trang roast pork is rich — eat a lot of it and it gets heavy, which is exactly why locals have it with dim sum and strong coffee. The famous shops don't all taste the same either: some lean sweet, some lean savory. Try a few and you'll find the one that suits you.

faq.q: Which Trang roast pork shop is the best?
faq.a: Locals rate Ko Phao in the municipal fresh market as the most famous of all — crisp skin, sweet juicy meat — but it sells out very fast. If you'd rather sit and eat in peace without a queue, Trang Moo Yang on Huai Yot Road is a long-running shop that's tasty and open long hours.

faq.q: What time do Trang roast pork shops open?
faq.a: Most open very early. The market vendors start around 6am and are sold out before 10–11am. Some, like Ban Bua Bok or Tha Do, open from 5:30am. If you're a late riser, aim for the longer-hour shops like Trang Moo Yang, Pong O-Cha or Ko Kuang instead.

faq.q: Roughly how much does Trang roast pork cost?
faq.a: Small plates start around 80–120 THB, and by the kilo it runs about 400–700 THB depending on the shop. The famous market vendors cost a bit more, while shops outside town like Tha Do are more wallet-friendly.

faq.q: Why do Trang locals eat roast pork in the morning?
faq.a: It's a Trang tradition mixed with Chinese-style dim sum culture. Locals get up and sit down at a dim sum shop, ordering roast pork with tea or coffee as breakfast — not as an evening drinking snack like elsewhere.

faq.q: Can I take Trang roast pork home as a gift?
faq.a: Yes. Many shops vacuum-pack it and ship nationwide. If you're taking it far, ask the shop for the ship-ready pack. The classic local pairing to bring back is Trang Chinese pastry.
